title: Noor and the Vector
premise: Astrid Eastwick smuggles stolen memories in sealed neural shunts past the customs ring of Halcyon Station, and alone she tends a navigation beacon whose original commissioning records have been erased. When the colony's children begin dreaming the same dream — a countdown, a door, two voices arguing behind it — Astrid discovers the beacon is a lock, and the dream is its key turning. The station's founders split humanity's survivors between an orbital elite who fled into cryosleep and a surface workforce left to endure; the reactor now finishing its countdown can wake only half. Astrid must choose which half wakes, and in doing so learns the beacon was built by her own forgotten self as insurance against exactly this choice. She refuses the binary, burning her smuggled archive of ten thousand memories to power a third option that wakes everyone slowly, at the cost of every memory she has ever carried, including her own name.
about_author: Sebastian Sterling is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical manuals for deep-space relay systems before turning to fiction. They live off-grid with a decommissioned weather satellite they insist on calling 'colleague.'

chapters.title: Contraband of the Mind
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She runs a shipment of black-market memories past customs hidden in a coffin of frozen dead, establishing her trade, her cynicism, and her quiet ritual of maintaining the orphaned beacon. Emotional beat: competent loneliness, a woman who trusts cargo more than people.

chapters.title: The Children's Dream
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Dockworker Maren begs Astrid to look at her son's neural scan: he dreams a reactor countdown, and so do forty other children, in perfect synchrony. Astrid recognizes the dream's imagery from the beacon's architecture. Beat: unease curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Beacon, Unclaimed
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV at the beacon array. She finds maintenance logs signed in her own handwriting from years she cannot account for, gaps in her own memory where payments should be. Beat: the first crack in her identity — the smuggler discovers she is also a mystery.

chapters.title: Customs Chief Voss
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. The customs chief suspects Astrid of the children's 'infection' and offers a trade: immunity for the beacon's access codes. Voss reveals the founding families still sleep in the deep vaults, and their lawyers want the beacon silent. Beat: predatory charm, power circling.

chapters.title: What the Shunts Carry
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Examining her own inventory, she finds one shunt she never recorded acquiring: inside it, a fragmentary memory of standing before the beacon's console while someone screams. Beat: fear of herself, the past pressing through the seal.

chapters.title: The Dream Spreads
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The dream jumps to adults; the colony clinic overflows with people waking at 3 a.m. reciting the same numbers. Maren's son draws the beacon perfectly, though he's never seen it. Beat: communal panic, tenderness under strain.

chapters.title: Vault of the Founders
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Under pressure from the sleeping families' proxy council, Voss raids Astrid's safehouse and seizes her shunt inventory. Astrid escapes through the coolant ducts with only the anomalous shunt. Beat: betrayal, the law revealed as the rich's long arm.

chapters.title: Two Voices Behind the Door
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Playing the anomalous shunt, she experiences the full memory: two founders arguing over the wake-order protocol — wake the vault elites or the surface workers — before the reactor's countdown locks the choice behind the beacon. One voice is hers. Beat: vertigo, grief, the self she lost.

chapters.title: The Countdown Is Real
chapters.summary: Engineer Okonkwo's POV. He confirms the reactor's decay curve matches the children's dream-numbers exactly: seventy-one days until the cryo-vaults fail and everything sleeps forever unless woken. Beat: cold clarity, the clock made flesh.

chapters.title: Market of Stolen Selves
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She seeks her old fence, Ilya, in the station's underdeck to decode who wiped her memory. Ilya names the proxy council's fixer, Serath, and warns that Voss has put a price on her head. Beat: loyalty among thieves, warmth in the margins.

chapters.title: Serath's Offer
chapters.summary: Serath's POV. The fixer offers Astrid restoration of her missing years in exchange for opening the beacon to wake the vault families first. He shows her a recording of herself volunteering for the wipe — willingly, to make the choice fair by forgetting it. Beat: seduction of wholeness, poisoned gift.

chapters.title: Maren's Bargain
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The proxy council detains the dreaming children for study. Maren, desperate, agrees to help Voss find Astrid in exchange for her son's release. Beat: maternal guilt, ordinary people ground between powers.

chapters.title: The Beacon Speaks
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Using the children's synchronized dream as a living key, she opens the beacon's buried layer: a message from her past self explaining the wipe and warning that any single choice will corrupt whoever makes it. Beat: communion across time with oneself, terrible inheritance.

chapters.title: Seventeen Days
chapters.summary: Okonkwo's POV. Recalibration shortens the deadline; panic riots hit the underdecks. Voss declares martial law and moves to seize the beacon by force. Beat: accelerating collapse, systems failing faster than trust.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Array
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Voss and Maren corner her at the beacon. Astrid shows Maren the truth of the children's dream; Maren turns on Voss, buying Astrid minutes with her body between them. Beat: sacrifice, an ordinary courage that changes the odds.

chapters.title: The Corruption of Voss
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Offered the beacon's master key by Serath, Voss takes it and quietly plans to wake only those who will owe him — the corruption theme embodied. He orders the vaults prepped and the surface workers locked out. Beat: ambition devouring principle.

chapters.title: Ilya's Price
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Ilya sells Astrid's location to Serath but secretly passes her the decryption shard she'll need, choosing friendship over survival. He is taken by Voss's men. Beat: love expressed as betrayal-and-gift, the cost of loyalty.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, climax begins. At the console with hours left, she holds the master key: wake the vaults, wake the surface, or let the reactor decide. She understands why her past self wiped the memory — no one should carry this choice intact. Beat: the weight of power fully arrived.

chapters.title: Burning the Archive
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, climax. Instead of choosing, she feeds her entire contraband archive — ten thousand smuggled memories, including her own recovered years — into the beacon as auxiliary power, enabling a slow-wake protocol that revives everyone gradually. Beat: transcendence through loss, the price paid in selfhood.

chapters.title: Waking
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The vaults open in staggered waves; the first founders emerge confused into a colony that no longer needs their permission to exist. Voss is arrested by his own deputies when the key proves worthless. Beat: reckoning, the powerful waking powerless.

chapters.title: Noor
chapters.summary: Okonkwo's POV. A child asks the nameless woman tending the beacon what she's called; she reads the beacon's old designation — NOOR, light — and accepts it. Fragments of her past return secondhand, told by strangers whose memories she once carried. Beat: identity rebuilt from community rather than archives.

chapters.title: The Third Door
chapters.summary: Astrid/Noor's POV, resolution. Months later, the station runs on shared memory-trust instead of hoarded secrets; the children's dream has become a lullaby. Noor keeps the beacon lit, not as a lock but as a promise, and begins recording new memories — freely given this time. Beat: peace earned, survival's price transmuted into gift.
